newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban says captures hilltops from opposition.
newsitem.headline: Taleban says captures hilltops from opposition.

text.p: A Taleban commander said on Sunday his forces had captured some hilltops from the opposition.
"We have captured some hilltops on the western side of the valley. Our positions now overlook the opposition on the valley floor," said Taleban commander Maulawi Ghulam Sakhi on Sunday morning.

Sakhi, speaking at an artillery position near the village of Hussein Kot, some 12 miles (21 km) north of Kabul, made the remarks amid a general stalemate between the Taleban and the opposition alliance north of Kabul, with no major movements by either side.
As he spoke, Taleban multiple rocket launchers were firing salvo after salvo into opposition-held territory. The sporadic rattle of small-arms fire could be heard in the distance.

The rockets raised huge plumes of dust as they landed. An opposition plane flew high over the front lines and dropped a number of bombs in the hills on the western side of the Shomali valley. It was not possible to ascertain if the bombs hit their target.
It was impossible to verify Sakhi's comments.
There has been little substantial movement in the front line since the opposition moved towards Kabul more than two weeks ago.
Both sides have launched minor offensives to regain territory. Some villages have changed hands a number of times during the two weeks.

Analysts in Kabul expect the opposition to launch an attack on Kabul as soon as it has repaired a broken bridge that is blocking the main supply route to the opposition heartland in the north of the country.
The opposition forces are commanded by Ahmed Shah Masood, who achieved almost legendary status in the guerrilla war against the communists.

"Once Masood has repaired the bridge he will be able to bring his heavy weapons to bear on the battle front. At the moment everything has to be hand-carried over the bridge," said the analyst, who wished to remain anonymous.
The opposition currently control a narrow salient of territory around the western road running south from the foothills of the Hundu Kush mountains to Kabul.
